title: Career Roadmap: Insurance Analyst
summary: An Insurance Analyst evaluates insurance policies, customer and claims data, risk exposure, pricing information, and business performance to help insurers make informed decisions. With a B.Sc. in Actuarial Science, you can build a strong foundation in probability, statistics, financial mathematics, risk modelling, and insurance operations.

blocks.text: This role can be a starting point for careers in insurance analytics, underwriting, claims analytics, risk management, and actuarial work.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: An Insurance Analyst and an Actuary are not interchangeable roles. An analyst may assess risk and insurance performance without being a qualified actuary. Becoming an actuary generally requires progressing through the relevant professional examination and experience pathway.

Project 2 — Claims risk analysis
Explore the factors associated with claim frequency or claim severity using an appropriate dataset.

blocks.label: Skills

Project 3 — Potential claims anomaly detection
Develop a prototype that flags unusual records for further human review.

blocks.label: Skills

Project 4 — Insurance portfolio comparison
Compare hypothetical insurance portfolios using exposure, claims, premium, and loss-ratio measures.

blocks.label: Skills

For each project, document the business question, dataset, assumptions, calculation methods, findings, and limitations. Make it clear that portfolio projects are educational analyses—not professional pricing or underwriting recommendations.

blocks.text: In India, the Institute of Actuaries of India publishes the professional examination and qualification pathways. Its current education policy describes the requirements for Associate and Fellow qualifications.

You do not need to qualify as an actuary for every Insurance Analyst role. Choose professional examinations based on your intended specialisation and the requirements of target employers.

blocks.text: Progress depends on experience, qualifications, professional requirements, and the responsibilities of the role.

Salary depends on the employer, city, analytical skills, product specialisation, and whether the position is an entry-level analyst or an actuarial trainee. Rather than assigning a universal salary figure, compare current vacancies for the exact job title and experience level.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Begin with probability, statistics, insurance fundamentals, and Excel. Then add SQL and Power BI, complete a claims-analysis project, and pursue an internship. If you enjoy advanced mathematical modelling, consider the actuarial qualification pathway as a separate long-term specialisation.
